title.narrative: Strengthening integrated Water Management in Syr Darya and Narin River Basins project

description.narrative: E.1 Knowledge Management and Communication 216. This Project Document adopts the GEF definitions for ‘knowledge’ and ‘knowledge management (KM) [45]. Knowledge management involves a strategic and multidisciplinary approach. This includes a series of activities that address key issues of the project, with a strong emphasis on integrating gender perspectives to address gaps and drive change. The project’s KM strategy is twofold: the SDB Child Project dimension which focuses on leveraging project experience to support learning and policy updates among project target audiences. 217. The second dimension is the linkage with the CAWLN coordination project, which will establish the framework for knowledge management across the region and facilitate the exchange of best practices and lessons learned among the five countries. The six CAWLN Child Projects (CPs) will contribute knowledge products in best practices, and lessons learned to the Coordination child project, which will serve as the primary hub for knowledge-sharing across all projects. This project will ensure that its M&E processes feed into this platform, and relevant outputs (e.g. case studies, reports) will be shared with IW:LEARN and other GEF platforms. The Coordination child project, on the other hand, will take the lead in consolidating and disseminating knowledge across all country projects, acting as the main interface with IW:LEARN and organizing regional knowledge-sharing events and capacity-building activities. It will also maintain the central platform for coordinating inputs and results from all projects. 218. In terms of communication, the project will ensure the effective dissemination of knowledge and best practices which will be supported by the development of a gender-sensitive communication strategy. The communication strategy will focus on sharing and publicizing project results to partners, stakeholders and general society. The objective is to enlarge project visibility, results and new initiatives implemented in the field, seeking to promote project credibility, transparency and legitimacy. 219. The project communication strategy will focus on both project implementation itself by facilitating effective communication within the project team and with project main partners, and publicizing project actions and results to the broader public by sharing its contributions, advancements, lessons learned and good practices to encourage replication and scaling up. 220. During the execution of capacity building and awareness raising activities, the project will consider the distribution of communication materials (flyers, cards, etc.) related to the Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) policies developed by FAO. All of this is framed within the Zero-Tolerance Policy of the United Nations System Toward Gender-Based Abuse and Violence, including sexual harassment, abuse and exploitation. E.2 Socio-economic Benefits and Decent Rural Employment [46] 221. This project aims to deliver significant socio-economic benefits at regional, national and local levels. At regional level the project will strength policy coordination and dialogue amount the riparian countries with the goal to enhance environmental and social sustainability by promoting the harmonious integration of water and land management practices. At national level, the project will promote ecosystem services and social society participation in planning and decision making, which will further support the country's commitment to biodiversity conservation and climate resilience. 222. Additionally, the project will have tangible socio-economic impacts at the local level, particularly for rural communities where agricultural productivity and livelihoods are threatened by unsustainable practices and environmental degradation. By supporting investments in sustainable land and water management and strengthening community-based resource management, the project will create job opportunities and generate income for local populations. Additionally, promoting biodiversity-friendly practices and enhancing resilience in agricultural systems will ensure food security and economic stability for rural households. 223. Social benefits include the empowerment of local communities through the involvement in water land nexus initiatives and process, enhance the understand of the importance of ecosystem services and biodiversity for the agriculture sector and its sustainability. Inclusive and participatory approaches will foster equitable distribution of the benefits derived from sustainable resource management, promoting social cohesion. Resilience and food security will be enhanced for vulnerable smallholders. 224. Furthermore, in project areas, the project will actively promote decent work and productive employment in rural areas, aligning with international labor principles. Through capacity-building activities, training programs, and the dissemination of best practices, the project will empower local communities to engage in sustainable agriculture and natural resource management practices, enhancing their livelihoods and overall well-being. Project actions align with Pillar 1 of FAO’s Decent Work Agenda [47], supporting employment creation and enterprise development. By fostering inclusive and participatory approaches, the project will ensure equitable distribution of the benefits derived from sustainable resource management, promoting social cohesion and economic development. The objective is to enhance water security and climate resilience in the Syr Darya and Narin River Basins by mainstreaming the Water-Land Nexus (WLN) through strengthening transboundary cooperation, advancing integrated watershed management practices and employing innovative monitoring technologies.
